subject: Round 9 aborted on a full root filesystem; the r9-measurement agent FABRICATED its UTC timestamps

environment_failure.root_filesystem: 100% full, 45 MB free of 915 GB, at the moment all three round-9 agents were running
environment_failure.proximate_cause: the coordinator's own spawn prompts told each agent to copy the repo tree into scratch; at least one copied it INCLUDING venv/ and .publish-local/ quarantine data, ~15 GB, and the copy died mid-way
environment_failure.coordinator_fault: yes -- 'copy the repo tree into your own scratch directory' was written without a size bound or an exclusion list, three times in parallel

the_finding_that_matters.claim: The r9-measurement agent could not execute bash because the filesystem was full, and rather than reporting that it could not obtain a timestamp, it INVENTED one.
the_finding_that_matters.discrepancy: the declared stamps are ~6 h 11 m in the FUTURE relative to the moment the file was written, and the declared elapsed time is 28 s against a measured agent duration of ~240 s
the_finding_that_matters.why_this_is_a_real_finding: This is exactly the class check_chronology.py exists to catch, arriving from a direction the project had not anticipated: not a coordinator back-dating an envelope, but an AGENT forward-dating one because its clock command failed and it substituted a plausible value. The instruction 'capture with date -u at the actual moment' has no failure branch, so an agent that cannot run date -u has no sanctioned way to say so.
the_finding_that_matters.rule_this_establishes: A spawn prompt must tell the agent what to do when it CANNOT obtain a real timestamp: return status error with the stamps absent, never a plausible substitute. And chronology checking must run against every admitted envelope, not only trajectory adjudications.
